# Nook

> Nook is a free, open-source Dynamic Island for Claude Code agents on Windows 10 and 11. It shows every running Claude Code session at the top of your screen, with approvals and answers from the island. It runs locally: no telemetry, no account, and no network use except an update check that is off until you switch it on. Version 0.2.2, MIT-licensed, by Zubair Bin Shaukat. Not affiliated with Anthropic.

Nook listens to Claude Code through its hooks and a small local relay (nook-hook.exe) over a named pipe. It never approves anything without a click and never blocks Claude Code. It also shows Cursor agent sessions next to Claude Code ones, status only (new in 0.2.0). Since 0.2.2 it also shows Codex sessions (with Allow and Deny) and lets you reply to a finished Claude Code or Codex session from the island.

## Guides

- [Install Nook on Windows](https://nook.zubyr.dev/guides/install/): Download, verify, install and uninstall Nook. SmartScreen, checksums and where the files live.
- [First run: hooks, shortcuts and a tour](https://nook.zubyr.dev/guides/first-run/): Install the Claude Code hooks, start a session and learn the island, the Shelf and the shortcuts.
- [How Nook talks to Claude Code](https://nook.zubyr.dev/guides/claude-code-hooks/): Hooks, the nook-hook relay and the named pipe: what is written to settings.json and what is never done.
- [Shelf widgets](https://nook.zubyr.dev/guides/shelf-widgets/): To-do, Timer, Reminders, Media, Mirror and Projects: what each does and what it keeps.
- [Cursor and Nook](https://nook.zubyr.dev/guides/cursor/): Cursor agent sessions next to Claude Code ones, status only, and how to turn them on.
- [Codex and Nook](https://nook.zubyr.dev/guides/codex/): Codex sessions next to Claude Code ones, Allow and Deny, replying from the island, and how to turn them on.
- [Troubleshooting Nook](https://nook.zubyr.dev/guides/troubleshooting/): SmartScreen, antivirus, a missing island, no sessions, shortcuts, camera and how to file a useful issue.
- [Nook FAQ](https://nook.zubyr.dev/guides/faq/): Plain answers on privacy, safety, hooks, signing, platforms and who makes Nook.
